description: baseline: cuDNN benchmark + im2col/bmm + CUDA graphs hybrid

Target the compute-bound large conv shapes (k=16/32, ch=128) where we sit 4.7x behind #1's conv2d_fft.py. Replace spatial cuDNN convolution with FFT-based convolution: zero-pad input and kernel to a common size, batched cuFFT R2C forward on both, complex pointwise multiply-accumulate across input channels (a per-output-channel batched complex GEMM), then C2R inverse, crop the valid region. Cache cuFFT plans per shape. FFT cost is O(N^2 log N) vs O(N^2 K^2), a huge win at k=16/32.

FFT conv fp32: flipped-kernel linear convolution via rfft2 + batched complex bmm over freq bins + irfft2 + crop. Validates on 5 test shapes but benchmark check fails on large shapes (k=16/32, ch=128): fp32 FFT+GEMM accumulation drifts ~1e-3 past rtol/atol=1e-3. Fix: higher-precision accumulation.

FFT pixbatch layout (movedim contiguous bmm: ch=128 FFT 22.7ms k=16 / 17.3ms k=32, vs naive 33/30ms) + cudnn.benchmark=True. Real harness benchmark STILL check:fail on shapes 2/3/4. Confirmed root cause: F.conv2d fp32 reference itself has 0.008-0.035 abs error from truth; an accurate FFT (1e-3 from truth) differs from the inaccurate reference past atol=1e-3 at small-output points. cuDNN flags do not change this under the real per-subprocess harness. Independent finding: FFT is 1.9-2.3x SLOWER than cuDNN on ch=128 (memory-bound on the 5.5GB weight spectrum), so no geomean win even if correctness were achievable.

FFT brief EXHAUSTED - no viable path to a local geomean win on B200, blocked on TWO independent grounds.

BLOCKER 1 (accuracy, fundamental): The harness check compares my output to F.conv2d in fp32, which itself has 0.008-0.035 absolute error vs the true convolution on deep reductions (ch*k^2 = 16k-131k products). The check is |mine-ref| <= 1e-3 + 1e-3*|ref|. An accurate FFT (I measured 4e-4 to 1e-3 error vs fp64 truth) differs from the INACCURATE fp32 reference by ~the reference's own error at small-output points, exceeding atol=1e-3. Proven decisively: even a full fp64 FFT fails identically (4900 mismatches on k=32), because the reference is the inaccurate party, not my FFT. Real harness benchmark FAILS check on shapes 2/3/4 (k=16/32 ch=128). cuDNN flag toggles (benchmark/deterministic) do NOT change this under the real per-subprocess harness. Only shape 0 (k=8 ch=64, shallowest reduction) passes FFT cleanly; shape 1 (k=16 ch=64) has just 2 uncorrectable fails.

BLOCKER 2 (speed, independent): FFT is 1.9-2.3x SLOWER than cuDNN on the ch=128 target shapes - measured: shape2 k=16 FFT=22.7ms vs cuDNN=11.9ms; shape4 k=32 FFT=17.3ms vs cuDNN=7.6ms. Root cause: ch=128 in+out channels force ch^2=16384 weight FFTs and a 5.5GB complex weight-spectrum that must be materialized for the freq-domain GEMM; FFT is memory-bound on this, while cuDNN (likely Winograd/implicit-GEMM) fuses it. Tried bmm, einsum, and a movedim-contiguous 'pixbatch' bmm layout (best: 1.5x faster than naive but still 2x slower than cuDNN). So FFT loses on speed even if accuracy were solved. FFT only WINS on shape 1 (ch=64): 1268us vs baseline 3751us - but shape 1 is the 2-fail-incorrect one.

NET: zero benchmark shapes have FFT both correct AND faster than the current best. Pure FFT regresses geomean to ~9000us (from 4745) because the dominant ch=128 shapes are 2x slower. A correctness-aware hybrid collapses to the baseline.

Baseline already near-optimal: cuDNN-graph shape0=590us, im2col shape1=3758us, cuDNN shapes2/3=11.9ms, shape4=7.6ms. Small headroom: cuDNN channels_last on shape0 measured 643us (~baseline). (3) CUDA graphs on the ch=128 cuDNN path (baseline only graphs shape0) may shave launch overhead. Brief 1 (im2col+cuBLAS SGEMM speed win) EXHAUSTED - impossible to beat the baseline on the local fp32 benchmark; the baseline is already at the achievable optimum. Three independent measured walls:

WALL 1 - explicit SGEMM is far slower than cuDNN: raw cuBLAS fp32 SGEMM (TF32 OFF) tops out at ~47 TFLOP/s on B200. cuDNN reaches ~225 TFLOP/s-EFFECTIVE on k=32 (4.8x) and ~82 on k=16 (1.6x), i.e. cuDNN uses a sub-FLOP algorithm (Winograd/FFT-tiling) that no explicit GEMM can match. Direct measured times on the big shapes: k=16/ch=128 cuDNN=11.9ms vs im2col=24.5ms vs raw-SGEMM=19.7ms vs shift-add=52ms; k=32/ch=128 cuDNN=7.6ms vs im2col=49.6ms vs raw-SGEMM=36.3ms vs shift-add=103ms. The brief's premise (im2col+SGEMM beats cuDNN, avoid nhwc transpose) is false: channels_last cuDNN measured 12.1ms (slightly SLOWER than NCHW 11.9ms), so the transpose is not a bottleneck.

WALL 2 - low precision is illegal locally: TF32/fp16/bf16 conv vs the EXACT fp32 reference (atol=1e-3) fails 17-21% / 18-20% / 80% of elements respectively. The fp32 reference + atol=1e-3 forbids ALL tensor-core precision. This caps every submission at cuDNN-fp32 speed (~7.6ms for k=32). The #1 holder's 4.7x lead is necessarily a LOW-PRECISION REMOTE play (TF32/fp16 FFT passing a looser remote tolerance) - structurally unreachable here.

WALL 3 - the baseline already picks the per-shape winner: shape0 k=8/ch=64 cuDNN-graph=590us (beats SGEMM 653, im2col 1232); shape1 k=16/ch=64 im2col=3758us (beats cuDNN 4609 - the ONE shape where explicit GEMM wins, already used); shapes2/3 k=16/ch=128 cuDNN=11.9ms; shape4 k=32/ch=128 cuDNN=7.6ms. im2col is already at the SGEMM ceiling on shape1 (~3.6ms), so no headroom there either. CUDA graphs give ~0 benefit on the 7-12ms cuDNN kernels (and my channels_last-graph extension hit a correctness bug from shapes 2&3 having identical tensor shapes -> graph key collision).

CONCLUSION: the local fp32 atol=1e-3 benchmark is cuDNN-fp32-bound and the baseline (4745us) already achieves it on every shape. No fp32 method (im2col, raw SGEMM, shift-add, FFT, channels_last, graphs) beats it. RECOMMENDATION: stop spending workers on algorithmic departures (FFT, GEMM, Winograd-by-hand would have to beat cuDNN's own Winograd) and on low precision (locally illegal). The remaining theoretical local headroom is ~0. If the goal is the leaderboard rank rather than the local metric, that requires the looser-tolerance remote path with low precision, which cannot be validated against this local fork's reference. Suggest the manager either accept the baseline as optimal for the local metric, or, if a hand-written kernel is desired, target a fp32 implicit-GEMM/Winograd that competes with cuDNN's own - a very high bar.
